newsitem.title: USA: Sunbeam says posted robust sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Sunbeam says posted robust sales growth.

text.p: Sunbeam Corp said Wednesday that the 13 percent sales growth in the first quarter was its highest without the benefit of acquisitions since going public in 1992.

It attributed its earnings growth in the quarter to the higher sales as well as restructuring efforts, under which it cut its workforce in half, reduced the number of factories to eight from 26 and decreased the number of warehouses to 18 from 61.
"The impressive growth in both revenue and earnings is proof that the revitalization of Sunbeam is working," Chairman and Chief Executive Albert Dunlap said in a statement.

In the first quarter, Sunbeam posted net income from continuing operations of $20.6 million, or $0.24 per share, on sales of $253.5 million. In the prior year's first quarter, Sunbeam posted net income from continuing operations of $6.7 million, or $0.08 per share, on sales of $229.7 million.
For the quarter, domestic sales from ongoing operations increased 12.5 percent, with growth achieved in every product category.
Sunbeam said gross margins for the quarter of 27 percent were six percentage points above those of the first quarter of 1996, while operating margins of 14 percent were double last year's level.
"The margins attained in the quarter are the highest achieved by Sunbeam in two years. I believe we are well on our way to achieving our goal of 20 percent operating margins," Dunlap said.
Dunlap said he expected a "tremendous number of growth initiatives instituted to drive further benefits throughout 1997."
